title: "I had strong faith while serving the country": Veteran shares National Day of Prayer testimony - NewsBreak
text:
By Ian Young Isaiah Calalang ,
1 hours ago
OWENSBORO, Ind. (WEHT) — The city of Owensboro is celebrating the 75th National Day of Prayer by welcoming a retired veteran who is most known for serving in the battle of Mogadishu.
It’s a battle most famously portrayed in the Academy Award winning film “Black Hawk Down.”
“The conversation went like this: ‘Hey I can’t tell you where I’m going, but I’m pretty sure I’m not going to be here on our wedding day,’” says Retired Army Ranger Major Jess Struecker. “And my wife’s response was, ‘Jeff, don’t play games with me. If you get shot, I want the flag. We need to get married before you leave.’”
Major Jeff Struecker takes the stage for the National Day of Prayer in downtown Owensboro. He’s most known for surviving the battle of Mogadishu and sharing that testimony for the 2001 film “Black Hawk Down.”
Now Struecker serves as a pastor turning a page from combat to faith.
“I had a very strong faith while serving the country,” says Struecker. “Being a man of prayer and a man who loves our country at the same time, for me, those two things were never a problem or a challenge.”
Owensboro residents like Lisa Trogden come from a military family and come out for the National Day of Prayer events every year. This year, her mother Ida Leachman tagged along to hear Struecker’s testimony.
“It means a lot,” says Trogden. “You know, it’s hard. My dad was just, you know, just did a couple of years in the military, but my husband’s 30 years. So, we know we want to take care of course.”
Struecker says he initially never wanted the film “Black Hawk Down” made. However, he says he’s proud of the contents of the film and since its release, he’s been able to share his perspective to communities all across the country.
“For me, this is kind of the best of both worlds,” says Struecker. “I get a chance to represent my brothers and sisters in uniform, but I also get a chance to see how incredible communities like Owensboro are.”
National Day of Prayer events continue Thursday morning with a veteran’s breakfast along the downtown Owensboro Riverfront followed by a prayer and worship service on the Daviess County Courthouse Lawn.
